architectural_implications.after: Model emits code/tool calls to zoom, adjust contrast, and re-inspect, producing an inspectable action trace.
architectural_implications.before: Hardcoded CV stages (detect → crop → OCR → parse) with tuned thresholds before the model sees anything.
architectural_implications.consequence: Perception failures become debuggable as wrong tool sequences, and image-processing logic can be changed by prompt/tooling rather than code deploys — but adds latency and nondeterminism to what used to be a deterministic stage.
architectural_implications.observation: Perception is reframed as agentic tool use rather than a fixed preprocessing pipeline.

architectural_implications.after: A router dynamically selects which tokens are processed deeply and which are skipped, so compute tracks information density.
architectural_implications.before: Every token in a long multimodal context costs the same forward-pass FLOPs.
architectural_implications.consequence: Cost and latency scale with content rather than raw context length; the router becomes a new single point of failure and a new thing to evaluate for recall loss.
architectural_implications.observation: Compute allocation is routed per token rather than applied uniformly.

architectural_implications.after: A slow semantic orchestrator plans and a separate tactile control policy executes real-time low-level control.
architectural_implications.before: One model end-to-end maps observation to action at a single update rate.
architectural_implications.consequence: Requires an explicit contract (state, goals, safety envelope) between tiers, and separate SLIs for plan quality versus control stability.
architectural_implications.observation: Control is split into orchestrator and tactile policy tiers.

architectural_implications.after: Retain dense text aggressively and compress/sample sparse perceptual streams selectively.
architectural_implications.before: Truncate or summarize context uniformly by token count.
architectural_implications.consequence: Context managers need per-modality policies and eviction rules, plus observability into what was dropped to explain downstream misses.
architectural_implications.observation: Modality-specific context management replaces uniform context handling.

article_ideas.angle: Take the two failure poles (dense-but-low-information pixels, sparse-but-high-information transcripts) and argue that teams scaling models are optimizing the wrong axis; make the case through attention-allocation reasoning and the concrete cost of a million-plus visual tokens per hour of video.
article_ideas.audience: ML engineers and research leads training or fine-tuning multimodal models
article_ideas.based_on: Traditional objectives like predicting transcripts or raw pixels suffer from severe sparsity or poor attention allocation.
article_ideas.thesis: In multimodal and agentic systems the binding constraint is supervision information density, not parameter count: dense pixel prediction burns capacity on predictable detail while transcript-only supervision under-trains attention on the events that matter, so objective design should be treated as an architectural decision.
article_ideas.title: Your Model Isn't Too Small — Your Training Objective Is Wrong

article_ideas.angle: Argue from the asymmetry that an hour of video costs millions of tokens while carrying poor ground truth, versus cheap dense text; derive concrete policy rules for screenshots, logs, telemetry, and frames, and show why uniform truncation and uniform summarization both lose.
article_ideas.audience: Engineers building long-running agents, context managers, and memory systems
article_ideas.based_on: Always-on cameras and robots create extreme context bloat where video is sparse and text is dense.
article_ideas.thesis: Allocating context by token count silently overprices dense text and underprices perceptual streams; context managers should budget by information density per modality, which means per-modality retention, compression, and eviction policies plus observability into what was dropped.
article_ideas.title: Token Budgets Are the Wrong Unit for Agent Context

article_ideas.angle: Reframe sparse routing as context selection: the router decides what the model never sees, and mis-routing shows up only as downstream task failure, which is invisible in average-accuracy reporting. Propose audit instrumentation and degraded-mode thresholds.
article_ideas.audience: Architects of agent runtimes and inference infrastructure
article_ideas.based_on: Data sparse architectures allow models to naturally model data sparsity and allocate compute dynamically.
article_ideas.thesis: Learned compute allocation is a legitimate answer to input sparsity, but it converts a cost problem into a recall problem that never raises an error — so sparse routing must ship with recall audits for rare-but-decisive tokens, not just FLOPs savings charts.
article_ideas.title: The Router Is a Silent Failure Mode

article_ideas.angle: Compare a fixed detect-crop-OCR-parse stage against an inspectable action trace on debuggability, latency, and cost, and give criteria for which stages deserve agency.
article_ideas.audience: Applied CV and document/OCR pipeline engineers moving to agentic stacks
article_ideas.based_on: Classical CV tasks can be reframed as agentic tasks where the model writes code, zooms in, and adjusts contrast.
article_ideas.thesis: Moving zoom, crop, and contrast adjustment out of hardcoded preprocessors and into the model's action space makes vision failures debuggable as wrong tool sequences and removable by prompt/tooling change — but the trade is added latency and nondeterminism, so agentifying perception should be a per-stage decision rule, not a migration.
article_ideas.title: Perception Should Be a Trace, Not a Pipeline

connections.relationship: Reframes vision preprocessing as an inspectable sequence of tool invocations, making perception subject to the same tracing and eval harness as other agent tools.

connections.connects_to: Context management and memory eviction in long-running agents
connections.relationship: Token-level routing is a learned alternative to heuristic truncation/summarization for deciding what enters the context window.

connections.concept: Information-density asymmetry (sparse video vs dense text)
connections.relationship: Suggests budgeting by information per token rather than tokens, changing how caching and compression are prioritized per modality.

connections.concept: Orchestrator vs tactile control policy split
connections.connects_to: Planner/executor separation and latency-tiered agent architectures
connections.relationship: Same pattern as slow reasoning layer plus fast deterministic executor, with distinct safety envelopes and evaluation criteria.

connections.connects_to: Reward and supervision design for agent traces
connections.relationship: If supervision signal density drives attention allocation, then harness design (what is labeled and logged) is an architectural lever, not a data-cleaning afterthought.

evidence_quotes.text: Traditional objectives like predicting transcripts or raw pixels suffer from severe sparsity or poor attention allocation.
Requires natural perceptive objectives rather than dense pixel prediction.

core_insights.generalization: Applies to any long-horizon agent: supervision that rewards dense low-value tokens wastes capacity, and supervision that only labels sparse high-value events under-trains attention. Objective design should match information density of the input stream.
core_insights.insight: The bottleneck in embodied/agentic perception is the training objective, not model capacity: predicting raw pixels gives dense but low-information supervision, while transcript-only supervision is sparse — both produce poor attention allocation. The fix is a different class of objective ('natural perceptive objectives') rather than a bigger model.
core_insights.why_it_matters: If the objective is the limiting factor, teams that keep fine-tuning bigger VLMs on caption/pixel-prediction losses are investing in the wrong axis; harness and data-curation design (what supervision signal is produced) dominates.

evidence_quotes.text: Always-on cameras and robots create extreme context bloat where video is sparse and text is dense.
1 hour of video requiring millions of visual tokens with poor ground truth.

core_insights.generalization: Generalizes to any agent ingesting screenshots, logs, or continuous telemetry alongside text: cheap text should be retained generously, expensive perceptual streams aggressively compressed or selectively sampled.
core_insights.insight: There is a structural information-density asymmetry in always-on multimodal context: video is token-expensive but information-sparse (roughly a million-plus visual tokens per hour with poor ground truth), while text is token-cheap and information-dense. Context budget should therefore be allocated by information density, not by token count.
core_insights.why_it_matters: Motivates per-modality retention/compression policies in agent memory and context managers instead of uniform truncation or uniform summarization; a token budget spent on video is not equivalent to the same budget spent on text.

evidence_quotes.text: Data sparse architectures allow models to naturally model data sparsity and allocate compute dynamically.
Significantly reduces compute costs while focusing attention on high-density information.

core_insights.generalization: Any agent with heterogeneous input streams (tool outputs, logs, frames, retrieved chunks) can apply learned routing to decide what to process deeply versus skip, rather than fixed pipelines.
core_insights.insight: Data-sparse mixture-of-experts routing is proposed as the direct architectural answer to input sparsity: instead of spending uniform compute per token, a router allocates dynamic compute so FLOPs track information content, which simultaneously addresses context bloat and cost.
core_insights.why_it_matters: Suggests sparse routing belongs at the token/context-selection layer, not only inside the FFN — i.e., which tokens get processed at all is a first-class design decision that changes both latency and cost profiles.

evidence_quotes.text: Classical CV tasks can be reframed as agentic tasks where the model writes code, zooms in, and adjusts contrast.

core_insights.generalization: Same pattern applies beyond robotics: OCR, chart reading, screenshot understanding, and document parsing become agentic tool sequences with inspectable intermediate artifacts instead of fixed preprocessing.
core_insights.insight: Perception itself becomes an agentic orchestration problem: instead of a fixed CV pipeline, the model writes code, zooms in, and adjusts contrast as tool calls. Classical vision tasks are reframed as multi-step tool-use episodes.
core_insights.why_it_matters: Moves responsibility for image processing out of hardcoded preprocessors and into the model's action space, making perception debuggable as a trace of tool calls rather than an opaque CNN stage.

evidence_quotes.text: Embodied reasoning separates orchestrator models from tactile control policies.

core_insights.generalization: Maps onto agent runtimes generally — a reasoning planner and an execution layer with different cycle times and safety envelopes — and argues against collapsing them into one call path.
core_insights.insight: Embodied reasoning is decomposed into a slow semantic orchestrator (embodied reasoning model) and fast low-level tactile control policies, rather than one model emitting motor commands directly.
core_insights.why_it_matters: Establishes a latency-stratified boundary: planning/reasoning model and real-time controller have different update rates, failure semantics, and evaluation criteria, so they should be separately versioned and monitored.

evidence_quotes.text: Embodied foundation models unify perception, reasoning, and action.
Reduces architectural fragmentation across robotic systems.

core_insights.generalization: Recurs across agent engineering: more capability is being absorbed into one model call, with orchestration moved inside the model rather than into framework glue code.
core_insights.insight: The strategic claim is consolidation: a single embodied foundation model covering vision, language, action, and world representations replaces separate VLM + VLA + world-model components, reducing architectural fragmentation while enabling zero-shot multi-step physical tasks.
core_insights.why_it_matters: If true, integration boundaries in robotics/agent stacks shift from inter-model APIs to internal routing, changing how teams version, evaluate, and swap components.

evidence_quotes.text: Traditional objectives like predicting transcripts or raw pixels suffer from severe sparsity or poor attention allocation.
1 hour of video requiring millions of visual tokens with poor ground truth.

deep_dives.research_question: Which training objective produces measurably better attention allocation than dense pixel prediction or sparse transcript prediction on the same multimodal data, and at what cost in labeled supervision?
deep_dives.topic: Objective design as the real bottleneck: what replaces pixel and transcript prediction
deep_dives.trigger_insight: Traditional objectives like predicting transcripts or raw pixels suffer from severe sparsity or poor attention allocation.
deep_dives.why: If the objective rather than capacity is the limiting factor, then compute spent on bigger VLMs is misallocated; the team that finds an objective with the right information density per token wins on both cost and grounding. Without a concrete loss/target definition, 'perceptive objectives' remains a slogan that cannot be implemented or falsified.

evidence_quotes.text: Data sparse architectures allow models to naturally model data sparsity and allocate compute dynamically.
1 hour of video requiring millions of visual tokens with poor ground truth.

deep_dives.research_question: Does dynamic per-token compute allocation skip rare-but-decisive perceptual evidence over long horizons, and can a cheap audit signal detect that skip before downstream task failure?
deep_dives.topic: Silent recall loss in token-level sparse routing
deep_dives.trigger_insight: Data sparse architectures allow models to naturally model data sparsity and allocate compute dynamically.
deep_dives.why: The claimed benefit is cost and focus; the unmeasured risk is that the router becomes a silent single point of failure whose errors never surface as exceptions, only as wrong answers. If rare frames are systematically dropped, any agent built on this architecture has an invisible reliability ceiling that standard accuracy averages will hide.

evidence_quotes.text: Always-on cameras and robots create extreme context bloat where video is sparse and text is dense.
1 hour of video requiring millions of visual tokens with poor ground truth.

deep_dives.research_question: Does allocating context budget by information-per-token rather than raw token count improve downstream task performance at fixed cost versus uniform truncation or uniform summarization?
deep_dives.topic: Per-modality context budgeting by information density
deep_dives.trigger_insight: Always-on cameras and robots create extreme context bloat where video is sparse and text is dense.
deep_dives.why: A uniform token budget implicitly prices a cheap dense text token the same as an expensive sparse video token, which is the wrong exchange rate. Per-modality retention and eviction policies are a concrete architectural lever that changes cost, latency, and what the agent can recall, and they need observability into what was dropped to explain misses.

evidence_quotes.text: Classical CV tasks can be reframed as agentic tasks where the model writes code, zooms in, and adjusts contrast.

deep_dives.research_question: On accuracy, latency, and cost, when does perception-as-tool-calls (write code, zoom, adjust contrast) beat a tuned fixed CV pipeline, and what does the extra nondeterminism cost in production?
deep_dives.topic: Agentic perception versus tuned classical vision pipelines
deep_dives.trigger_insight: Classical CV tasks can be reframed as agentic tasks where the model writes code, zooms in, and adjusts contrast.
deep_dives.why: Reframing perception as tool use makes failures debuggable as wrong tool sequences and lets image logic change without a code deploy, but it converts a deterministic stage into a multi-step, latency-added, nondeterministic one. Teams need a decision rule for which perception stages to agentify, not a blanket migration.

evidence_quotes.text: Mk1 is an embodied foundation model trained on >1 Petabyte of text, images, videos, and trajectories, outperforming Gemini 3.1 Pro on embodied reasoning while being 15x cheaper.

deep_dives.research_question: Under an independently specified benchmark and cost accounting (tokens, hardware, latency), does the reported embodied-reasoning advantage over a general frontier model hold, and what does the 15x figure actually include?
deep_dives.trigger_insight: outperforming Gemini 3.1 Pro on embodied reasoning while being 15x cheaper
deep_dives.why: A single-vendor comparative claim with no named benchmark, protocol, or cost boundary is not decision-grade evidence, yet it is exactly the kind of number that gets quoted in build-versus-buy decisions. Reproducing or refuting it determines whether specialization is a real economic moat or a benchmark artifact.

project_ideas.hypothesis: On identical multimodal data and a fixed FLOP budget, a region/event-grounded perceptive objective yields lower attention entropy and higher downstream task accuracy than dense pixel prediction or transcript-only prediction.
project_ideas.measurement: Attention entropy over semantically annotated events, downstream task accuracy on held-out multi-step inspection tasks, and supervision cost per labeled example across the three arms at matched FLOPs.
project_ideas.name: Objective Bake-Off Harness
project_ideas.poc: Build a three-arm training harness over one fixed video/telemetry corpus: (a) raw-pixel prediction, (b) transcript/caption prediction, (c) region- or change-grounded prediction with tool-invoked inspection traces. Hold parameters and token budget constant and log per-layer attention entropy plus downstream probe scores.

project_ideas.based_on: Always-on cameras and robots create extreme context bloat where video is sparse and text is dense.
project_ideas.hypothesis: Allocating context budget by estimated information density per modality beats uniform token-count truncation and uniform summarization on downstream task success at equal total token cost.
project_ideas.measurement: Task success rate at fixed total tokens, plus drop-recall: fraction of retained key facts/events that were present in the source stream and survived eviction, with per-policy eviction traces for failure explanation.
project_ideas.name: Per-Modality Context Eviction Policy
project_ideas.poc: Implement a context manager with pluggable policies (uniform truncation, uniform summarization, density-weighted retention with aggressive perceptual sampling and generous text retention) over sessions mixing screenshots, logs, and text. Run all policies against the same long-horizon task suite with a fixed token ceiling.

project_ideas.based_on: Data sparse architectures allow models to naturally model data sparsity and allocate compute dynamically.
project_ideas.hypothesis: Learned token-level sparse routing skips a measurable fraction of rare but task-decisive frames that dense attention retains, and this skip is detectable by injected canary frames before it appears as task failure.
project_ideas.measurement: Canary retention rate versus dense baseline, downstream accuracy on canary-only queries, compute savings, and the gap between canary-retention warnings and observed task failures.
project_ideas.name: Rare-Frame Router Recall Audit
project_ideas.poc: Construct long perceptual streams seeded with labeled canary frames carrying the only evidence needed to solve a downstream query. Compare router-based selection against dense-attention baselines at matched compute and instrument whether canaries are selected, deferred, or dropped.

project_ideas.based_on: Embodied reasoning separates orchestrator models from tactile control policies
project_ideas.hypothesis: Splitting an embodied agent into a slow semantic orchestrator and a fast tactile/execution policy with an explicit state-goal-safety contract yields more stable control and clearer failure attribution than a single end-to-end observation-to-action loop, at equal task success.
project_ideas.measurement: Control stability (variance of execution commands), task success under planner stalls, end-to-end latency distribution per tier, and fraction of failures attributable to plan quality versus control instability.
project_ideas.name: Two-Tier Latency Contract Simulator
project_ideas.poc: Build a simulated task loop with a scripted slow planner (variable, occasionally stalling) and a fast deterministic executor. Run conditions: single-tier baseline, two-tier with defined contract, two-tier with planner stalled mid-task. Instrument tier-level traces.

summary.html:
Overview

  • Speaker: Armen Aghajanyan
  • Channel: AI Engineer
  • Main topic: Embodied foundation models, physical AI, and multi-modal architectures for robotics and agentic perception.
  • Purpose: Explain the transition toward embodied foundation models and discuss research findings, architectures, and scaling laws for physical AI systems. Armen Aghajanyan, Co-founder and CEO of Perceptron, discusses the evolution from traditional VLM and VLA models to Embodied Foundation Models that unify perception, reasoning, and action. He highlights fundamental challenges like weak traditional training objectives and context bloat in multimodal models, presents Perceptron's data-sparse mixture of experts approach and Mk1 model, and demonstrates emergent agentic capabilities in robotic tasks.

Topic Map

Introduction to Embodied Foundation Models

  • Explanation: Defining Perceptron's mission to bridge the physical and digital worlds through real-time perception, understanding, and interaction.
  • Key claims:
    • Embodied foundation models unify perception, reasoning, and action.
    • Intelligence must be brought to any device, instrument, robot, camera, or sensor.
  • Examples:
    • VLMs, VLAs, pixel world models, and semantic world models.
  • Terminology:
    • Embodied Foundation Models
    • Physical AI
    • VLMs
    • VLAs
  • Why it matters: Unifying modalities enables a single model to perceive, reason, and control physical systems.

Two Fundamental Research Challenges

  • Explanation: Addressing the challenges of weak traditional training objectives and context bloat in multimodal models.
  • Key claims:
    • Traditional objectives like predicting transcripts or raw pixels suffer from severe sparsity or poor attention allocation.
    • Always-on cameras and robots create extreme context bloat where video is sparse and text is dense.
  • Examples:
    • 1 hour of video requiring millions of visual tokens with poor ground truth.
  • Terminology:
    • Context Bloat
    • Sparse Training Signals
    • Token Compression
  • Why it matters: Solving data sparsity and context length bottlenecks is essential for scalable physical AI.

Data-Sparse Architectures and Mk1

  • Explanation: Using mixture of experts and sparse routing to let models dynamically compute per token, leading to the release of Mk1.
  • Key claims:
    • Data sparse architectures allow models to naturally model data sparsity and allocate compute dynamically.
    • Mk1 is an embodied foundation model trained on >1 Petabyte of text, images, videos, and trajectories, outperforming Gemini 3.1 Pro on embodied reasoning while being 15x cheaper.
  • Examples:
    • Visualizing compute allocation on fruit stands and graphs.
  • Terminology:
    • Data-Sparse Mixture of Experts
    • Mk1
    • Token Routing
  • Why it matters: Enables efficient scaling and context management for real-time robotic applications.

Embodied Reasoning as Orchestration and Demos

  • Explanation: Examining how embodied reasoning orchestrates agentic systems, task annotation, and robotic execution.
  • Key claims:
    • Classical CV tasks can be reframed as agentic tasks where the model writes code, zooms in, and adjusts contrast.
    • Embodied reasoning separates orchestrator models from tactile control policies.
  • Examples:
    • Robot assembling parts, reading book titles, and sorting into bins.
  • Terminology:
    • Agentic Perception
    • Tactile Control Policy
    • Orchestrator
  • Why it matters: Demonstrates complex multi-step robotic tasks operating zero-shot in real-world environments.

Key Points

Unified Multimodal Modeling

  • Explanation: Embodied foundation models integrate vision, language, action, and pixel/semantic world representations into a single unified architecture.
  • Evidence: Diagram showing perception, reasoning, and action loops inside a single embodied model.
  • Practical implication: Reduces architectural fragmentation across robotic systems.

Weak Objectives in Video Modeling

  • Explanation: Predicting raw pixels or relying solely on sparse transcripts leads to poor attention allocation and inefficient training.
  • Evidence: Comparison of dense text tokens vs. sparse video tokens in 1 hour of video.
  • Practical implication: Requires natural perceptive objectives rather than dense pixel prediction.

Context Bloat and Sparse Architectures

  • Explanation: Continuous video input from robots generates huge context lengths, which can be handled using sparse mixture of experts routing.
  • Evidence: Data-sparse mixture of experts paper allowing dynamic compute per token.
  • Practical implication: Significantly reduces compute costs while focusing attention on high-density information.

Frameworks, Models & Processes

Embodied Foundation Model Framework

  • How it works: Unifies perception, reasoning, and action within a single model architecture handling text, images, video, and trajectories.
  • Components:
    • Perceive
    • Reason
    • Act
    • Grounding
    • Representations
  • When to use: When building physical AI systems requiring real-time interaction with the physical world.

Data-Sparse Mixture of Experts

  • How it works: Uses routing mechanisms to allow models to dynamically select which tokens to process and which to skip.
  • Components:
    • Token Router
    • Expert Layers
    • Dynamic Compute Allocation
  • When to use: When processing long-context multimodal inputs like continuous video streams.

Examples & Case Studies

Robot sorting books into bins based on reading titles.

  • Illustrates: Multi-step tasks combining perception, OCR, and robot control.
  • Lesson: Embodied models can handle complex perception and control loops zero-shot.

Actionable Takeaways

  • Immediate:
    • Explore public APIs and benchmarks for Perceptron models.
    • Investigate data-sparse mixture of experts for multimodal context management.
  • Strategic:
    • Shift from fragmented VLMs/VLAs to unified Embodied Foundation Models.
    • Leverage scaling laws combining teleoperation data with internet-scale video.
  • Questions to investigate:
    • How to further improve temporal and spatial reasoning robustness in robotic control?
    • What is the optimal mixture ratio for teleop vs. pre-training video data?

Claims Worth Verifying

  • Mk1 outperforms Gemini 3.1 Pro on embodied reasoning and is 15x cheaper. (Performance Benchmark Claim)
  • Mk1 was trained on >1 Petabyte of text, images, videos, and trajectories. (Training Scale Claim)

Notable Quotes

"We build Physical AI to perceive, understand, and interact with the physical world in real-time" (at 0:40) "Embodied foundation models unify perception, reasoning, and action" (at 1:53)

Compressed Summary

  • Embodied foundation models unify perception, reasoning, and action.
  • Traditional video training objectives suffer from sparsity and poor attention allocation.
  • Data-sparse mixture of experts enable dynamic compute per token and solve context bloat.
  • Mk1 achieves frontier embodied reasoning performance at significantly lower cost.
  • Keywords: embodied ai, foundation models, mixture of experts, robotics, multimodal
  • Core insight: Embodied foundation models trained with data-sparse architectures can bridge digital and physical worlds efficiently by unifying perception, reasoning, and action into a single model.

### Two Fundamental Research Challenges
- **Explanation**: Addressing the challenges of weak traditional training objectives and context bloat in multimodal models.
- **Key claims**:
  - Traditional objectives like predicting transcripts or raw pixels suffer from severe sparsity or poor attention allocation.
  - Always-on cameras and robots create extreme context bloat where video is sparse and text is dense.
- **Examples**:
  - 1 hour of video requiring millions of visual tokens with poor ground truth.
- **Terminology**:
  - Context Bloat
  - Sparse Training Signals
  - Token Compression
- **Why it matters**: Solving data sparsity and context length bottlenecks is essential for scalable physical AI.
### Data-Sparse Architectures and Mk1
- **Explanation**: Using mixture of experts and sparse routing to let models dynamically compute per token, leading to the release of Mk1.
- **Key claims**:
  - Data sparse architectures allow models to naturally model data sparsity and allocate compute dynamically.
  - Mk1 is an embodied foundation model trained on >1 Petabyte of text, images, videos, and trajectories, outperforming Gemini 3.1 Pro on embodied reasoning while being 15x cheaper.
- **Examples**:
  - Visualizing compute allocation on fruit stands and graphs.
- **Terminology**:
  - Data-Sparse Mixture of Experts
  - Mk1
  - Token Routing
- **Why it matters**: Enables efficient scaling and context management for real-time robotic applications.
### Embodied Reasoning as Orchestration and Demos
- **Explanation**: Examining how embodied reasoning orchestrates agentic systems, task annotation, and robotic execution.
- **Key claims**:
  - Classical CV tasks can be reframed as agentic tasks where the model writes code, zooms in, and adjusts contrast.
  - Embodied reasoning separates orchestrator models from tactile control policies.
- **Examples**:
  - Robot assembling parts, reading book titles, and sorting into bins.
- **Terminology**:
  - Agentic Perception
  - Tactile Control Policy
  - Orchestrator
- **Why it matters**: Demonstrates complex multi-step robotic tasks operating zero-shot in real-world environments.
## Key Points
### Unified Multimodal Modeling
- **Explanation**: Embodied foundation models integrate vision, language, action, and pixel/semantic world representations into a single unified architecture.
- **Evidence**: Diagram showing perception, reasoning, and action loops inside a single embodied model.
- **Practical implication**: Reduces architectural fragmentation across robotic systems.
### Weak Objectives in Video Modeling
- **Explanation**: Predicting raw pixels or relying solely on sparse transcripts leads to poor attention allocation and inefficient training.
- **Evidence**: Comparison of dense text tokens vs. sparse video tokens in 1 hour of video.
- **Practical implication**: Requires natural perceptive objectives rather than dense pixel prediction.
### Context Bloat and Sparse Architectures
- **Explanation**: Continuous video input from robots generates huge context lengths, which can be handled using sparse mixture of experts routing.
- **Evidence**: Data-sparse mixture of experts paper allowing dynamic compute per token.
- **Practical implication**: Significantly reduces compute costs while focusing attention on high-density information.
## Frameworks, Models & Processes
### Embodied Foundation Model Framework
- **How it works**: Unifies perception, reasoning, and action within a single model architecture handling text, images, video, and trajectories.

  - Representations

### Data-Sparse Mixture of Experts
- **How it works**: Uses routing mechanisms to allow models to dynamically select which tokens to process and which to skip.

- **When to use**: When processing long-context multimodal inputs like continuous video streams.
